newsitem.title: GREECE: LOW INFLATION, RATES TO DRIVE GREEK SHARES - CARNEGIE.
newsitem.headline: LOW INFLATION, RATES TO DRIVE GREEK SHARES - CARNEGIE.

text.p: Greek equities will benefit from the virtuous circle of falling inflation and interest rates and the stock market will resume its uptrend this year, said Carnegie International in its March research report.

"We continue to believe that the rise will continue since the overall picture is unchanged: inflation continues its downward course, interest rates are falling and the government shows no let up in the implementation of its strict fiscal policy," it said.
Despite the market's correction recently, the uptrend will continue given the favourable fundamentals.
"The virtuous circle will be good for the stock market and we expect interest rates to be a significant driver of equities this year," it said.

Greece enjoyed a month of positive macroeconomic news, as lower inflation in February -- 6.6 percent -- built on January's gains and enabled the government to push official interest rates and T-bill rates lower.
The European Commission has also published fully harmonised inflation data for the full 15-member EU for the first time.

"On this calculation, Greek inflation was just 6.6 percent in January rather than the 6.8 percent recorded by the national index. This underlines both the progress made and the scope for future progress," Carnegie said.
Greek shares were up 2.35 percent at 1,325.78 points close to mid-session on Friday.
